author: Ankit
problem: Read N people standing in a line, given as P_1..P_N where P_i is the person at position i from the front, then Q queries of two person numbers A and B. For each query, print whichever of the two people stands further to the front.
bug_description: Marks position j as ahead of position i instead of person P[j] ahead of person P[i], so it answers as if person k stood at position k.

comments.accurate: Answers each query with whichever of the two people is closer to the front of the line
comments.wrong_behavior: Person numbers follow the line order, so the smaller number is always further to the front
comments.wrong_location: Ahead-of table verified; check that the query numbers are converted to 0-based indices
